content.comment_body: Hello! I am unable to see the [product_name] menu with [article_no] on the web server or manage it from the server. The server only displays the elements of the [product_name] (see attached file), and I can't interact with them. Any guidance with a practical example would be appreciated.
In this topic: [url] I mentioned to you that the webserver can only show message texts, and not the menus of the [product_name].
For reference, please see the attachment.
Thank you, things are starting to make sense now. This is actually what I was aiming for, but how can I control the inputs or outputs (like I1, I2, Q1, Q2, etc.) that are used in my program?
Could you please describe precisely what you want to achieve?

I set up a small test with the [product_name] and [article_no] on the training bench (see attached file). Inputs I1, I2, I3, and I4 are connected to sensors; outputs Q1 and Q2 are connected to lamps. The system works when different sensors are physically activated. Now, I want to control the system from the web server—how can I do this?

Through the web server, you cannot switch inputs or outputs directly (forcing). Outputs could only be managed if they are not handled by the program using variables. If you want web-based control, you'll need to use the virtual keys on the [product_name] and/or the [product_name] operator device. You must create message texts via the menu and link the buttons accordingly. There is a helpful document attached, which offers a basic overview, though it is not complete.
Thank you. I'll try to study your example in detail and review my own challenges. Thanks again, as your assistance has helped broaden my understanding of automated systems!

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to remotely control and monitor inputs and outputs on a [company_name] [product_name] ([article_no]) using its web server. There is confusion about what functions the web server actually supports—specifically, real-time hardware interaction. The forum clarifies that direct remote control of inputs and outputs isn't supported through the web interface, which only allows for message text display, not menu or control functions. This results in some user frustration and misunderstandings regarding the system's capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to be able to view and interact with the [product_name] menus, inputs, and outputs remotely from the web server, mimicking physical interaction with the device.
